items.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022
items.q: Well I had a friend doing my website and PR stuff for many years, Deb Lake

ctx.x: I’d like to focus on two terms he used, “mainstream” and “post-bop.” He called you a post-bop saxophonist, which I don’t think you’d necessarily argue with as far as a timeline, but do you describe your playing with terms like that? If you could write a review of yourself what terms would you use to describe your playing?

Well I had a friend doing my website and PR stuff for many years, Deb Lake, and she came up with a little blurb to go with me and with my label Renma Recordings, and she said, “jazz with a twist.” So it’s pretty straight-ahead but we’re not playing standards all the time and we’re not playing, you know, other people’s arrangements, and I think with mainstream, I mean mainstream has changed as I’m sure you know. So it’s a little bit of a © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

tricky thing. But when I think of mainstream I think of not really what’s happening now in jazz, with all the young people. And I’d love to talk to you about all that also, but I mean I’m not a free player, but I’m not totally mainstream. But I have elements of mainstream. So that’s what I really like when she said, “jazz with a twist.” It’s — like we play songs, whether they’re originals or whatever, with melodies and it’s just — but then we do things like some odd meters and the last chunk of years I’ve been…
